issues.legal_issue: A municipal improvement scheme for providing building sites is authorized only when forming or altering streets is expedient for that purpose, not when the scheme merely acquires land to develop and sell plots or houses.
material_facts: The scheme involved acquiring land, laying it out, and selling plots or plots with houses to the public.
The scheme was not for forming new streets or altering existing streets to provide building sites.
issues.conclusion: The scheme was not authorized on the street-formation ground, and the Chief Executive Officer was not competent to notify its making on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: Section 277(1)(B) permits an improvement scheme where forming or altering streets is expedient for the purpose of providing building sites for the city's expansion; it does not authorize a scheme whose purpose is simply to develop and sell plots or houses. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: improvement_scheme_authority_dispute and scheme_develops_and_sells_land and not street_changes_for_site_creation

predicates.improvement_scheme_authority_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether a municipal improvement scheme was authorized.
predicates.scheme_develops_and_sells_land: The municipal authority proposed to acquire land, develop it, and sell plots or plots with houses to the public.
predicates.street_changes_for_site_creation: The municipal authority proposed to form or alter streets to provide building sites.

issues.definition: When a municipal improvement scheme develops and sells land without forming or altering streets to provide building sites, the scheme is not authorized.

issues.legal_issue: A scheme to provide plots or houses for middle-class purchasers does not qualify as a scheme to construct buildings for the accommodation of the poorer and working classes.
material_facts: The scheme envisaged making plots available to middle-class people or selling them houses built by the Corporation at a cost of about Rs. 7,500 each.
The area was to be developed and sold to the public on a no-loss, no-profit basis.
The scheme did not provide for construction of buildings to accommodate indigent working people unable to arrange reasonable accommodation themselves.
issues.conclusion: The scheme was not for the purpose of constructing buildings for the accommodation of the poorer and working classes.
issues.legal_principle: Section 277(1)(A)(c) concerns construction of buildings to accommodate indigent and working people who cannot arrange reasonable accommodation themselves; it does not cover merely providing plots or selling buildings to purchasers able to acquire such housing. The Court relied on the ordinary meanings of “middle class,” “working class,” and “poor” in Webster's New World Dictionary. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: improvement_scheme_authority_dispute and housing_for_middle_income_buyers and scheme_offers_plots_or_completed_homes and not accommodation_for_indigent_workers

predicates.improvement_scheme_authority_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether a municipal improvement scheme was authorized.
predicates.housing_for_middle_income_buyers: The municipal authority intended the housing to be available to middle-income purchasers.
predicates.scheme_offers_plots_or_completed_homes: The municipal authority proposed to provide plots or sell completed houses rather than construct buildings to accommodate the intended residents.
predicates.accommodation_for_indigent_workers: The municipal authority proposed to construct buildings for indigent working people unable to arrange reasonable accommodation themselves.

issues.definition: When a scheme serves middle-income buyers by offering plots or completed homes rather than accommodation for indigent workers, it is not a scheme for the poorer and working classes.

issues.legal_issue: Notifications and acquisition proceedings dependent on an improvement scheme whose originating notification was unauthorized are invalid.
material_facts: The later notifications and the Land Acquisition Officer's order related to the scheme initiated by the first notification.
The first notification was not authorized because the scheme did not fall within the statutory purposes for which an improvement scheme could be made.
issues.conclusion: The subsequent notifications and the Land Acquisition Officer's order were invalid, and the acquisition proceedings could not stand.
issues.legal_principle: The later notifications were invalid because they referred to a scheme whose origin was not justified by the Act; acquisition proceedings could not be valid when their underlying notifications were invalid. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.acquisition_proceeding_challenge: The proceeding challenges notifications and an acquisition order relating to a municipal improvement scheme.
predicates.originating_scheme_notice_unauthorized: The initial notice for the scheme was issued even though the scheme did not fall within the authorized purposes for making such a scheme.
predicates.later_notices_and_order_depend_on_scheme: The later notifications and acquisition order related to the scheme initiated by the initial notice.

issues.definition: When an acquisition challenge concerns later notices and an order dependent on an unauthorized originating scheme notice, those notices and the acquisition proceedings are invalid.
